findings.description: X-Road is open-source data exchange layer software. Prior to 7.8.2, 7.7.3, and 7.6.4, HashChainVerifier in the common-message module resolves attacker-controlled batch-signature hash chains before verifying the message signature and signing certificate, without cycle detection, recursion-depth or total-step limits, or per-step memoization. A registered ecosystem member can send a small crafted hashchain MIME part with repeated or cyclic StepRef values so that verifyHashChain() performs exponential work or unbounded recursion before authentication. Repeated requests can exhaust Security Server proxy threads and deny data-exchange service, and a self-reference can raise an uncaught error. This issue is fixed in versions 7.8.2, 7.7.3, and 7.6.4.

A flaw was found in the Ansible language server shipped with the vscode-ansible extension. The regular expression used to extract documentation fragments from Ansible module files is susceptible to quadratic-time scanning. A module file containing a crafted documentation string causes the language server to consume excessive CPU while indexing it, freezing the language service in the developer's editor. An attacker who can get a developer to open or index a workspace containing an attacker-supplied collection can cause a denial of service of the editor language features. This issue has no confidentiality or integrity impact.

A flaw was found in ansible-builder. The regular expression used to strip comments from a collection's requirements.txt during introspection is susceptible to super-quadratic backtracking. A requirements file containing a line with a long run of internal whitespace and no comment character causes the comment-stripping routine to consume CPU time proportional to the square of the line length. An attacker who can get a victim to build an execution environment that includes an attacker-supplied collection can cause the ansible-builder build or introspect process to hang, resulting in a denial of service. This issue has no confidentiality or integrity impact.

The rsyslog's`imuxsock` special parser can end up writing into the received message raw buffer when trying to replace the message timestamp with the system's timestamp. A local attacker with the ability to write to the `imuxsock` socket can leverage that by crafting a malformed PRI value with a short timestamp to lead the rsyslog to perform the out-of-bounds write.

X-Road is open-source data exchange layer software. Prior to 7.8.2 and 7.7.3, the Configuration Proxy uses attacker-controlled Content-location metadata from a validly signed federated global configuration part when constructing an output path without verifying that the resulting path remains inside the intended configuration output directory. A malicious or compromised federated ecosystem can provide an absolute path or directory traversal sequence during the normal refresh cycle, causing the Configuration Proxy to create a new file with attacker-controlled content under the permissions of the non-privileged xroad process. The vulnerability can poison downstream global configuration or create files in other writable locations, but it does not overwrite existing files. This issue is fixed in versions 7.8.2 and 7.7.3.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

erofs: disable LZ4 rolling decompression for now

LZ4 rolling decompression [1] was introduced to reduce the memory
footprint of temporary pages:

 For many cases, it is needed for users to read small data within
 a compressed extent (pcluster), either due to random small read, or
 since uptodate folios (typically order-0) cannot be reused for
 decompression again since decompression algorithm refills
 already-uptodate folios.

Rolling decompression works because LZ4 is LZ77-based and only refers
to the most recent 64 KiB of decompressed data, so in theory only a
bounded rolling window of temporary pages is needed when decompressing.

It can save a lot of temporary memory, e.g.
 601,960-byte data can be compressed into a 256k LZ4 compressed extent,
 which means it needs 146 extra pages per request in the worst case if
 rolling decompression is disabled.

However, the upstream LZ4 implementation is not under EROFS' control:
For example, the literal copy memmove() may still **copy long literals
backward** on x86 based on the address comparison even when the source
and destination ranges do not overlap (IOWs, inline decompression
doesn't need to be considered here). That breaks the rolling assumption
and makes the optimization broken.

Disable it for now to make sure the data correctness first since EROFS
is used everywhere now: The rolling window approach can be revived once
we either ensure that the official LZ4 code always copies forward for
non-overlapping ranges or maintain our own LZ4 implementation in EROFS.

The main impact is a higher runtime memory footprint; However, recent
commit 0f6273ab4637 ("erofs: add a reserved buffer pool for lz4
decompression") helps mitigate this when enabled but it's still not
perfect.

[1] https://www.usenix.org/conference/atc19/presentation/gao
    § 3.3 Decompression

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ring-buffer: Add checking nr_subbufs to persistent ring buffer validation

Sashiko reported that the code was using meta->nr_subbufs without making
sure that it matched the nr_pages + 1 on data that was assuming the two
were the same.

Add a check to the persistent ring buffer validation code to make sure
that the saved nr_subbufs matches what we expect.

Command injection vulnerability in the affected interface of AOS-10 or AOS-8 could allow an authenticated remote attacker to perform command injection only on certain impacted devices. Successful exploitation could allow an attacker to execute unauthorized arbitrary commands with the privileges of the affected mechanism on the underlying operating system.

An unauthenticated buffer overflow vulnerability exists in the underlying operating system of AOS-10 or AOS-8 and could allow an unauthenticated adjacent attacker to conduct a denial of service attack. Successful exploitation could allow an attacker to disrupt the availability of the affected system, with a limited impact to the integrity of the affected component.

Vulnerabilities in the PAPI protocol of AOS-10 could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to circumvent existing authentication controls. Successful exploitation could allow an attacker to gain administrative access, modify system configurations, and access or manipulate sensitive data.

Mattermost versions 11.11.x <= 11.11.0, 11.7.x <= 11.7.11, 11.10.x <= 11.10.2 fail to check whether the calling session originated from an OAuth authorization grant, which allows a third-party application holding a delegated access token to register a new, independent OAuth application under the identity of the delegating user via the OAuth application registration endpoint.. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00780

Poppler through 26.11.0 contains an uncontrolled memory allocation vulnerability in the libcurl-based remote file loader that trusts unvalidated HEAD Content-Length values in CurlCachedFileLoader::init(). Malicious HTTP servers can return an enormous Content-Length so CachedFile resizes its chunk cache accordingly, aborting pdfinfo or PDFDocFactory-based applications with std::bad_alloc for denial of service.

The Flamix: Bitrix24 and WooCommerce Products Sync WordPress plugin before 1.7.0 does not restrict or validate an unauthenticated file-exchange request, allowing anyone to write a file with an attacker-chosen name, extension and path to a web-served location and thereby execute arbitrary PHP.

The RSVP and Event Management WordPress plugin before 2.7.19 does not sanitise and escape attendee data imported from a spreadsheet before outputting it on the frontend RSVP form, which could allow users with the Author role and above to perform Stored Cross-Site Scripting attacks against anyone, including administrators, viewing the affected attendee, even when the unfiltered_html capability is disallowed.

The Hide My WP Ghost  WordPress plugin before 7.0.19 does not remove or restrict a debug branch in its output rewriting, allowing unauthenticated attackers to reveal the hidden login page, the hidden admin path and the renamed content folders the Hide My WP Ghost  WordPress plugin before 7.0.19 is meant to conceal.

The Hide My WP Ghost  WordPress plugin before 7.0.19 only enforces two-factor authentication on the interactive login flow and not on other authentication paths, allowing an attacker who already has a user's valid password to authenticate as that user without completing the second factor.

The ProfilePress  WordPress plugin before 4.18.1 does not atomically consume the source subscription when processing a membership plan change, allowing a customer to submit concurrent plan-change checkouts against a single paid subscription and obtain several active memberships for the price of one.

The Otter Blocks  WordPress plugin before 3.2.10 does not use URL-aware escaping when it resolves its dynamic data tags inside HTML attributes, which could allow unauthenticated users to post comments containing links that execute arbitrary JavaScript when clicked, for example by a logged-in administrator.

The Contact Form 7 WordPress plugin before 6.2.5 does not check that the post a form submission says it was sent from is publicly viewable before resolving post-related mail-tags, allowing unauthenticated users to obtain the title, URL, author name and author email of private, draft and trashed posts where such tags are used in an email or message returned to the submitter.

The WPvivid — Backup, Migration & Staging WordPress plugin before 0.9.140 does not prevent serialized data it cannot safely unserialize from being re-serialized as a PHP object during a site migration, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber to plant a PHP object that WordPress instantiates after an administrator restores a backup onto a different URL.

The WPvivid — Backup, Migration & Staging WordPress plugin before 0.9.140 does not limit its table prefix rewrite to table names when restoring a database backup, which corrupts the length of stored serialized values and allows users with a role as low as Subscriber to plant a PHP object that WordPress instantiates after an administrator restores a backup.

Description
When an HTTP profile and an iRule containing the PSC::ip_address command are configured on a virtual server, undisclosed requests can cause the Traffic Management Microkernel (TMM) to terminate and may lead to remote code execution (RCE).

Impact
Traffic is disrupted while the TMM process restarts. This vulnerability allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the BIG-IP system and may allow the attacker to perform RCE. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

The Dynific Addons for Elementor (formerly Anywhere Elementor) WordPress plugin before 1.3.1 does not perform a capability check on an AJAX action that stores a configuration value, allowing any authenticated user, including Subscribers, to store a value that is later output without proper escaping in a quoted attribute on an administrator settings page, resulting in Stored Cross-Site Scripting that executes in the administrator's session.

The Flatsome WordPress theme before 3.20.13 does not sanitise post meta saved through an AJAX action, nor escape it when rendering the product page, allowing users with a role as low as Contributor (who lack the unfiltered_html capability) to store JavaScript that executes in the browser of anyone who views the product, including administrators.

The Flatsome WordPress theme before 3.20.13 does not verify that the acting user is authorised to modify the target post when saving a template, allowing users with a role as low as Contributor to overwrite the content and type of an arbitrary post, including another user's published page, removing it from the front end.

The Flatsome WordPress theme before 3.20.13 does not perform a capability or nonce check on an AJAX action available to authenticated users, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber to disclose the name and content of non-public templates stored on the site.

The Search & Replace WordPress plugin before 3.2.4 does not restrict one of its database tools to network administrators on multisite installations, allowing administrators of a single subsite to run arbitrary SQL against the whole network's database and make themselves Super Admin.

The Royal Addons for Elementor  WordPress plugin before 1.7.1071 does not restrict or validate the post meta keys used when counting or rendering a filtered grid, and does not reject private (hidden) meta keys, allowing unauthenticated users to disclose the value of arbitrary private post meta one value at a time from the filtered result count. This is an incomplete fix of CVE-2026-17585, whose 1.7.1067 patch covered only a separate search-based path and left the grid filtering path affected.

The Envira Gallery  WordPress plugin before 1.16.4 does not apply its own gallery-permission policy until an administrator first opens its permissions screen, instead copying gallery-management capabilities onto each role from that role's core post capabilities after activation, which lets Contributor accounts create, edit and delete galleries that the policy is meant to restrict to higher roles.

The Link Library plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'linkfile[name]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 7.10.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires an administrator to have enabled the "Link File" option within the plugin's settings, which activates the vulnerable file upload field on the public add-link form.

A vulnerability in the phishcheck functionality of ClamAV could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause a DoS condition on an affected device.
 This vulnerability is due to improper allocation of memory during processing of URLs. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a URL to be processed by the software. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to cause the ClamAV scanning process to terminate, resulting in a DoS condition on the affected software.

A vulnerability in the Yoda'a Crytper (yC) Portable Executable (PE) unpacker of ClamAV could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause a DoS condition on an affected device. .
 This vulnerability is due to lack of proper error checking for negative values when processing the PE file to be unpacked. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a PE file to be unpacked. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to cause the ClamAV scanning process to terminate, resulting in a DoS condition on the affected software.

A vulnerability in the debug logging functionality of ClamAV could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause a DoS condition on an affected device.
 This vulnerability is due to improper handling of logging values. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by submitting a file to be scanned by the software that has debug logging enabled. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to cause the ClamAV scanning process to terminate, resulting in a DoS condition on the affected software.
